_meta.title: Where each NAMED augment is found — the wiki's own `locations` field
_meta.source: ddowiki.com, `{{Item Augment}}` infobox `locations` parameter on each augment's own `Item:<name>` page, batched MediaWiki API (action=query, prop=revisions, 20 titles per POST, ~1.5s apart) per docs/wiki-evidence/harvest-method.md
_meta.why: The Farming List's hunting list for augments. gear-planner carries no acquisition data for any augment (location_quest is empty on all of them), so without this the list could say which augment to slot but never where to get it.
_meta.shape:
Each `locations` line on the wiki is `Place + how + detail;`. `place` is linked by the wiki's own template to the page of that exact title; `how` is the wiki's own source kind (loot, rewards, purchasable augments, reward items); `detail` is the chest / cost text with wiki link markup reduced to its label and `
` to ` ; `.
_meta.population: Every augment in the catalog WITHOUT `acquirable` (the 472 named ones, per docs/wiki-evidence/augment-acquirability.md). The 675 acquirable (Common/Uncommon/Rare) augments are NOT harvested here: the rarity ruling already states where they come from (vendors, Mysterious Remnants, random chest loot), and all 675 were verified 2026-09-27 to be members of those categories at exactly `Item:<name>` (sha256 of the sorted stripped names equals that of the catalog's acquirable set).
_meta.no_page: 82 named augments — every one an `(Epic)` Solar or Lunar Gem — have no wiki page at `Item:<name>`. They are recorded with `page: null` and render with no link and no location, never a guessed one.
_meta.verification: The name list sent to the wiki hashed identically on both sides (sha256 897cc207…). The harvested payload was hashed in the browser before readback and re-hashed on disk (sha256 7a46500d…). All 112 distinct places were checked with prop=info and exist (Joe Candymaker redirects to The Night Revels).
